- Overestimate prices when sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, especially after recent spikes; reduce forecast peak values.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) or neutral (0.00), particularly if recent prices are trending downward; adjust downward bias.
- Overshoot after sharp upward moves in history — cap forecast peaks at 1.5–2x recent high if sentiment is positive but volatile.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is > 1.2x recent 7-day average, reduce by 10–20% unless sentiment strongly supports continuation.
- Lagged sentiment effect: if sentiment was bullish 3–5 days ago, reduce forecast by 5–10% to account for delayed reaction.
- Horizon-specific: for 30-day forecasts, avoid overconfidence in early days (1–7) — adjust downward if sentiment is mixed or negative.
- If sentiment is consistently positive but price declines, reduce forecast slope — avoid “sentiment-driven” momentum traps.
